newsitem.title: FRANCE: French jobless fund sees 13.6 bln Ffr '96 surplus.
newsitem.headline: French jobless fund sees 13.6 bln Ffr '96 surplus.

text.p: French national unemployment fund Unedic forecast on Thursday that it would post a 13.6 billion French franc ($2.66 billion) surplus for 1996 and an 11.7 billion franc surplus for next year.

The use of the 1996 surplus -- whether to lower payroll contributions or raise unemployment benefits -- will be a key issue in negotiations due to start at the end of November involving unions, employers and the state.
The surplus, along with deficits in the social security system, is included in calculating the total public deficit as defined by the Maastrict Treaty on Euroepan monetary union.
Last month, Unedic forecast a 12 billion franc surplus by the end of 1996.
The surplus marks a continuation of the turnaround in the fund's finances since it ran heavily into debt in the early 1990s.

Unedic uses payroll taxes to pay for unemployment benefits. It is operated separately from the social security system which covers pensions, healthcare and family benefits and which is running a big deficit.
Unedic statistics showed that the fund expected 1996 to show an increase of 120,000 in the number of job seekers in France.
The fund expects a 61,000 increase in the number of unemployed in 1997 and expects unemployment to stabilise in 1998.

Earlier on Thursday, official figures were released showing another 27,700 people joined France's jobless rolls in September -- almost double the amount forecast by economists -- pushing the country's unemployment rate to a record 12.6 percent.
